review_findings: The original r0_clean.py remains byte-identical. The new entry is independent and preserves the original output/runtime location to retain once-only scientific attempt markers.

The original SHA-checked device-injection adapter runs before the new bounded allocator adapter. Restoring exactly the gate import and cap assignment produces the original complete Backend AST. All model and rendering definitions remain unchanged.

The real Backend constructor bytecode contains a 12 GiB cap instead of 16 GiB. The original allocator-setting statement precedes load_models and decoder construction. A stub constructor test confirms cap installation precedes the stub model call without constructing any real model.
The DINO-only stage installs the same 12 GiB cap before its only MetricEvaluator construction. Its function AST matches the original after reversing only that cap constant.

The GPU admission, absolute runtime free memory, current-process reserved-credit limit, and policy evidence consistently use 15/2/12 GiB and a 14 GiB free-plus-own threshold. Host RAM, CPU, filesystem, GPU identity, and utilization checks remain unchanged.

The complete worker AST is restored by reversing only its call to adapt_backend_limited. plan, render_one, validate_source, validate_image, token_count, guard_for, owner and wait_child are unchanged. CAPS, MODELS, FLAGS, SIZES, OFFSETS and MISSING_STATES are unchanged.

Registration requires a pinned zero-science retirement receipt and absence or replacement identity of the original waiter. Prelaunch also rejects existing owner_launch, render, score, failure, actual_wait and complete scientific output markers. The original timing and owner locks and inherited-descriptor behavior remain unchanged.

No empty_cache, precision, batch-size, decoder, algorithm flag, token order, model weight, source population, budget or extra qualification call was added. A runtime scientific failure is preserved and is not automatically retried.
limitations: Historical same-model FP32 batch-one visual jobs reached 16066281472 bytes of PyTorch reserved memory. Their approximately 1.84 GiB inter-frame allocated value is not a peak-allocated measurement. This review therefore does not prove that 12 GiB fits.

The reduced allocator limit is a declared quality-experiment resource revision. Frozen source definitions and numeric flags are preserved, but no new bitwise-repeatability or memory qualification has been run or claimed.

The first actual scheduled frame must be part of the existing 5400-call budget. OOM or any other unknown scientific failure must stop and retain the original ledger and evidence; it is not authorization for automatic retry or an additional qualification frame.
This review does not change or qualify the six-method timing entry, R1 registration, or R2 gate.
